spacr.batch_correction.MAD_SCALE_ROUNDED:
R's rounded MAD constant (cellHTS2, Funk et al. 2022).

``sp_stats.MAD_SCALE`` is the full ``1 / Phi^-1(0.75)`` = 1.482602218...;
the two differ by about 1.5e-6 relative, so each caller of :func:`_scale`
names the one its output was built with.
spacr.measure.dna_phases:
The model-free DNA-content call of G1, S, G2, subG1, >4N and M (item 995).

The one entry point of the field-centred call: Measure's cell-cycle step
(:func:`_classify_cell_cycle`), the OPS cell-cycle phase
(:func:`spacr.ops_cell_cycle.run_cell_cycle_phase`) and the OPS profile
path all reach :func:`_field_centred_dna_phases` through it. It needs no
stage model, only the integrated DNA intensity of each nucleus, its
fit group (well) and its field (site).

:param cells: a frame with one row per cell, or the path of a cell table;
    a path is read for the needed columns only, through
    :func:`spacr.tabular.read_table_columns`.
:param dna: the integrated nuclear DNA intensity column.
:param group: the fit-group column, one fit per value.
:param field: the field column, nested in ``group``.
:param mitotic: the external M call: a boolean column name, a boolean
    array, or None for no external call (every cell is then fitted as
    non-mitotic and none is called M).
:param centre: centre every field on its G1 peak first.
:param min_cells: the non-mitotic cells a field needs to be shifted.
:param gates: optional ``[G1/S, S/G2]`` in DNA content units.
:param capture_diagnostics: retain exact fit populations for diagnostic
    reporting without changing phases, fitting or verdicts.
:param groups: ready-made ``(name, row positions)`` fit groups, for a
    caller that groups by more than one column; replaces ``group``.
:param fields: ready-made field label per row; replaces ``field``.
:returns: ``(frame, fits)`` of :func:`_field_centred_dna_phases`, the
    frame on the index of ``cells``; ``phase`` is G1, S, G2, subG1,
    >4N or M.
:raises ValueError: a column is missing.
spacr.ops_cell_cycle.import_stage_bundle:
Convert a development stage-model bundle to a release checkpoint folder.

:param path: the ``.joblib`` bundle read by :func:`stage_bundle`.
:param folder: the directory that receives the checkpoint.
:returns: the checkpoint directory of :func:`save_cell_cycle_checkpoint`; load it with
    :func:`load_cell_cycle_checkpoint`.
spacr.ops_cell_cycle.stage_bundle:
A development stage-model bundle (a ``.joblib`` dict), mapped onto :data:`CLASSES`.

The bundle holds ``format`` ``spacr-cellcycle-stage-model-1``, a ``model``, ``features``,
its own ``classes`` and a ``normalisation`` text. Classes that :data:`CLASSES` has and the
bundle lacks (``telophase_daughters`` in the six-class plate A model) get probability 0.
The bundle's own class names are matched to :data:`CLASSES` by name and the mapping is
written in the card. The normalisation must be the per-well robust z of
:func:`spacr.ops_mitotic._well_robust_z`, which :func:`predict_stages` applies.

Unpickling runs code, so the bundle is only as safe as its source; there is no checksum
file to check, so the SHA-256 of the file is recorded in the card instead.

:param path: the ``.joblib`` file.
:returns: ``{"model", "features", "training", "card", "sha256"}``, the shape of
    :func:`load_cell_cycle_checkpoint`.
:raises ValueError: for another format, a class :data:`CLASSES` does not know or another
    normalisation.
spacr.ops_settings.ops_setting:
One setting's value, ``OPS_DEFAULTS[key]`` when it is unset.

The one place a reader that may run without :func:`ops_defaults` having
filled the dict (an internal helper called on its own) takes the default
from, so no module carries a second default table. ``None`` and ``""``
count as unset.

:param settings: the settings mapping.
:param key: a key of ``OPS_DEFAULTS``.
:returns: the set value, or the declared default.
spacr.ops_tvn.batch_mean_sd:
Per-batch mean and population standard deviation, in two float64 passes.

The one routine behind every per-well centre-scale: the OPS TVN
(:func:`_centerscale_by_batch`) and the embedding robust-z/TVN
profiles (:func:`spacr.gene_measurement_compare._well_statistics`).
The first pass sums each batch's values, the second sums the squared
deviations from the batch mean, both in float64, so the variance does
not lose precision to ``E[x^2] - mean^2`` cancellation. Rows are read
``chunk`` at a time, so an embedding on disk never sits in memory whole;
the result differs from an in-memory call only by float64 summation
order. Non-finite values are ignored, as ``StandardScaler`` ignores NaN.

Zero-SD policy (``zero_sd``): ``'relative'`` gives SD 1 to a column
with no spread (SD zero, or at most :data:`ZERO_SD_RELATIVE` of the
size of its mean, which is rounding noise) or with no finite value, so
it is centred to 0 and never divided by a vanishing number;
``'exact'`` gives SD 1 only where the SD is exactly zero or not finite;
``'keep'`` returns the SD as computed, zeros included, for a caller
that drops constant columns itself.

:param embedding: the rows (an array or a memory map).
:param rows: the rows used, in order.
:param batches: the batch of each used row.
:param chunk: rows read at a time.
:param visit: called as ``visit(start, block)`` for every block of the
    first pass, so a caller can collect rows without a further read.
:param zero_sd: ``'relative'``, ``'exact'`` or ``'keep'``, as above.
:returns: ``(mean, sd)`` float64 arrays keyed by batch.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown ``zero_sd``.
spacr.ops_tvn.nuisance_covariates:
The per-cell covariates of the nuisance sources, one ``nz_*`` column each.

``cell_cycle`` is ``stage_probs`` (``p_<class>``, the first class
dropped, since the set sums to 1, with ``posterior_S`` and ``posterior_G2``)
plus ``dna_content`` (``dna_log2_fc`` and its square). ``mitotic_binary`` is one
interphase-versus-mitotic indicator, the mitotic cells kept, and ``phase_onehot`` the
S, G2 and M indicators of ``cell_cycle_stage`` against G1. ``size`` is the log cell and nucleus
areas; ``density`` the neighbour count and the log nearest-neighbour
distance; ``position`` the squared distance of the nucleus from the centre
of its field (the middle of the field's centroid range). ``field`` adds
``nz_field`` (well and site), which :func:`regress_nuisance` centres on.

:param cells: the cell table.
:param kinds: the sources, from :func:`nuisance_kinds`.
:returns: a frame row for row with ``cells``, float64 with gaps as NaN.
spacr.ops_tvn.nuisance_kinds:
The checked nuisance sources of ``ops_profile_nuisance``, in canonical order.

:param value: None or empty (off), one name, or a list of names from
    :data:`NUISANCE_KINDS`.
:returns: the chosen names, each once.
:raises ValueError: for a name that is not a nuisance source.
spacr.ops_tvn.nuisance_source_columns:
The cell-table columns the nuisance sources need, checked against the table.

:param cells_columns: the columns of the cell table.
:param kinds: the sources, from :func:`nuisance_kinds`.
:returns: the columns to read, in a stable order.
:raises ValueError: when a source finds none of its columns.
spacr.ops_tvn.regress_nuisance:
Remove the linear part of per-cell nuisance covariates from the features, in place.

Per feature, ordinary least squares with an intercept on the fit cells
(``control``), then ``x - [1 z] B`` for every cell. With ``fields`` each
field's mean of the features and of the covariates, taken over all of its
cells, is removed first (the field fixed effect), through the
centre of :func:`spacr.batch_correction._center`. Columns are processed in
blocks, float32 in place, with the normal equations accumulated in float64.

Gaps are safe: a gap in a feature leaves that cell's value a gap and drops
it from that feature's fit; a cell with a gap in any covariate is not
adjusted by the slopes (its covariates stand at the fit mean) and drops
out of the fit.

:param values: one float array per well, cells by features; changed in place.
:param covariates: one array per well, cells by covariates; may be empty.
:param control: one boolean array per well, the cells the slopes are fitted on.
:param fields: one label array per well, or None for no field effect.
:returns: ``{"covariates", "n_fit", "coefficients"}``: ``coefficients``
    is the ``(1 + covariates) x features`` matrix ``B`` of standardised
    covariates, with ``mean`` and ``scale`` of each covariate.
spacr.tabular.read_table_columns:
Read only some columns of one table, a chunk of rows at a time.

A Parquet file is decoded row group by row group, so the columns left out are never
brought into memory: a whole-well cell table of 2,800 columns costs only the few
columns asked for. Another format is read with its ``usecols`` or ``columns`` argument
through :func:`read_table`. Column names are kept as written, not canonicalised.

:param source: the table path.
:param columns: the column names wanted; a name the table lacks is skipped.
:param chunk_rows: rows decoded per chunk of a Parquet file.
:param table: the table name, for a database.
:returns: the frame with the wanted columns, in the order given.
spacr.utils.build_cellpose_model:
Build a Cellpose model the one way every caller builds it.

The steps, in order: a pinned model file recorded for ``key`` replaces
the name, the name is resolved by :func:`_resolve_cellpose_pretrained`,
the device and weight format come from
:func:`spacr.accelerator.cellpose_kwargs`, an explicit ``gpu`` or
``device`` overrides them, weights are float32 off the GPU, and
``mask_inference_precision`` in ``settings`` has the last word.

:param model_name: a stock or legacy name, a checkpoint path or a
    model-zoo name; blank is ``cpsam``.
:param settings: read for ``mask_inference_precision`` (``auto``,
    ``bf16`` or ``fp32``) and, with ``key``, for the pinned model file.
:param key: the setting that names the model; when ``settings`` pins a
    file for it, the file is loaded instead of ``model_name``.
:param object_type: 'cell' / 'nucleus' / 'pathogen' / 'organelle' for
    the messages.
:param restore_type: unsupported under Cellpose 4; reported and ignored.
:param setting: the field name the messages use, ``key`` when absent.
:param device: an explicit torch device overriding the accelerator's.
:param gpu: ``False`` builds on the CPU without asking the accelerator,
    ``True`` forces the card, ``None`` takes the accelerator's choice.
:param drop_device: leave the device to Cellpose, which follows ``gpu``.
:param float32_on_cpu: load float32 weights whenever the model runs off
    the card, whatever the accelerator reported.
:param tolerant: when the accelerator cannot be read, build on the CPU.
:param cache: ``cache(identity, factory)``, which returns a model kept
    for the session; ``identity`` names the resolved model and kwargs.
:param library_default: for the stock ``cpsam`` name, leave
    ``pretrained_model`` out so the installed Cellpose picks its own
    default weights, which is how the OPS wells were validated.
:param factory: the model class to construct, ``CellposeModel`` of the
    library when absent; a module passes its own import of it.
:returns: a ``cellpose.models.CellposeModel``.
:raises ModelZooError: if the name cannot be resolved exactly.
:raises ModelUnreadable: if downloads are disabled and the stock model
    is not cached.
spacr.utils.build_cellpose_model.constru: Load the model once the kwargs are settled.
